chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: Mavouzy's jealousy and reputation
summary: After Benny Waters left, saxophonist Robert Mavouzy of Guadeloupe, a brawler in the papers every weekend, was jealous of Butler, a foreigner.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: Now, when Benny got angry and left, and this Martinique boy's name, Mavouzy --
Yeah, could play. He was from Guadelupe.
Mavouzy (PHONETIC) was something else. But see, he was jealous.
How'd he get his name? Was he --
His name was Robert Mavouzy, M-a-v-u-z-y.

Yes. Strange name. And he had his friends, his countrymen--compatriots--and they would sit down and ---"get Jacques, Jacques is a foreigner." And he was working; he's got two jobs. So Mavouzy said, "I want you to take me down there with you." Well, the man had said, "Don't you bring Mavouzy down here because Mavouzy has been doing too many things. You know, Mavouzy got to fighting with a trumpet player and the trumpet player cut him on his buttocks. Mavouzy had some other woman cutting another woman's throat. Mavouzy was always doing something. He was in the paper every weekend. Mavouzy is a good saxophone player, but I don't want Mavouzy. Mavouzy'd have all my women fighting and going on. He's a handsome boy, by the way."
